question_text: How many days must a candidate wait before retaking a failed GAMB exam?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 90 days
options.D: 14 days

explanation: Rule 510-2-.01 provides that a candidate who fails the Georgia Jurisprudence Examination (GAMB) must wait at least 30 days before retaking the examination.

question_text: What exam must be passed before taking the GAMB jurisprudence exam?

options.A: The Georgia Board oral examination
options.B: EPPP (the national licensing exam)
options.C: Comprehensive Psychology Competency Examination (CPCE)
options.D: ABPP Specialty Board Examination

explanation: Rule 510-2-.01 requires passing the Examination for Professional Practice in Psychology (EPPP) prior to taking the Georgia jurisprudence exam (GAMB).

question_text: After passing the EPPP and GAMB, what is the third licensure exam?

options.A: EPPP Part 2 (Skills)
options.B: The National Psychology Jurisprudence Examination
options.C: The Georgia Board oral examination
options.D: Specialty Board Certification Examination

explanation: Under Rule 510-2-.01, after passing the EPPP and the GAMB jurisprudence exam, the final examination requirement for licensure is the Georgia Board Oral Examination.

question_text: How many days does an endorsement applicant have to petition after provisional license denial?

options.A: 45 days from the denial letter date
options.B: 30 days from the denial letter date
options.C: 90 days from the denial letter date
options.D: 60 days from the denial letter date

explanation: Rule 510-2-.01 provides that an applicant denied a provisional license has 60 days from the date of the notification letter to petition the Board.

question_text: How many days does an applicant have to respond to a Board request for additional information?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 15 days
options.C: 45 days
options.D: 60 days

explanation: Under Rule 510-2-.01, an applicant must respond to a Board request for additional information within 30 days or the application may be deemed abandoned.

question_text: How many members are on the Georgia State Board of Examiners of Psychologists?

options.A: Five members: four licensed psychologists and one public/consumer member
options.B: Six members: five licensed psychologists and one public/consumer member
options.C: Seven members: six licensed psychologists and one public/consumer member
options.D: Nine members: seven licensed psychologists and two public/consumer members

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-3 and Rule 510-1-.01 establish that the Georgia State Board of Examiners of Psychologists consists of six members: five licensed psychologists and one consumer/public member.

question_text: Who appoints members of the Georgia psychology board?

options.A: The Secretary of State
options.B: The Attorney General
options.C: The Governor
options.D: The President of the Georgia Psychological Association

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-3 provides that all members of the Georgia State Board of Examiners of Psychologists are appointed by the Governor.

question_text: What is the term length for Georgia psychology board members?

options.A: One year, serving until successors are appointed
options.B: Two years, serving until successors are appointed
options.C: Three years, serving until successors are appointed
options.D: Five years, serving until successors are appointed

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-3 specifies that board members serve five-year terms and until their qualified successors are appointed.

question_text: What immunity do Georgia psychology board members have?

options.A: No civil liability for acts performed in good faith in official duties
options.B: Qualified immunity from criminal prosecution only, with full civil tort liability
options.C: Absolute immunity covering intentional torts and gross negligence in the course of proceedings
options.D: Limited immunity that applies only if the Attorney General pre-approves each regulatory decision

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-2 provides that Board members have immunity from civil liability for acts performed in good faith in the performance of official duties.

question_text: How often must the board elect officers?

options.A: Biennially; president and secretary-treasurer
options.B: Annually; president and vice-president
options.C: Semi-annually; president and vice-president
options.D: Every five years concurrent with member terms

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-5 and Rule 510-1-.02 provide that the Board shall elect annually from its members a president and vice-president.

question_text: How many regular board meetings are required each year?

options.A: At least four
options.B: At least two
options.C: At least one
options.D: At least six

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-5 requires the Board to hold at least one regular meeting each year, though additional meetings may be called by the president or division director.

question_text: What does 'practice of psychology' require in Georgia?

options.A: Completion of an APA-accredited doctoral degree and registered internship only
options.B: A certificate of professional qualification from ASPPB without state registration
options.C: Enrollment in good standing with the Department of Behavioral Health
options.D: A valid Georgia psychology license

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-7 mandates that any person who wishes to engage in the practice of psychology in Georgia must obtain a valid license from the Board.

question_text: Who may use the title 'psychologist' in Georgia?

options.A: Only persons licensed under Chapter 39 (with limited exceptions)
options.B: Any individual holding a doctoral degree in psychology from an accredited university
options.C: Any professional licensed by the Georgia Composite Board of Professional Counselors
options.D: Any member in good standing of the American Psychological Association

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-17 restricts the use of the title 'psychologist' (or words implying licensure) strictly to individuals licensed under Title 43, Chapter 39, with limited statutory exceptions.

question_text: What is 'psychological testing' defined as?

options.A: The administration of paper-and-pencil self-report questionnaires for educational placement only
options.B: Use of assessment instruments to measure mental abilities, personality, or neuropsychological functioning and to diagnose/evaluate mental disorders
options.C: Any clinical intake interview conducted by a licensed behavioral health provider to establish a psychiatric diagnosis
options.D: The non-standardized observation of patient behavior used to design behavioral intervention plans

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-1(6) defines 'psychological testing' as the use of assessment instruments to measure mental abilities, personality, or neuropsychological functioning and to diagnose/evaluate mental disorders.

question_text: What is 'neuropsychological functioning'?

options.A: Medical evaluation of neurological reflexes and electroencephalography
options.B: Neurological disease pathology evaluated exclusively through diagnostic neuroimaging
options.C: Psychological manifestations of brain functioning
options.D: Cognitive performance measured solely during psychoeducational academic evaluations

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-1(5) defines 'neuropsychological functioning' as psychological manifestations of brain functioning.

question_text: What is 'mental abilities' in Georgia law?

options.A: Innate academic aptitudes measured exclusively by standardized school achievement tests
options.B: General cognitive intelligence quotients determined under standardized medical protocols
options.C: Neurological motor functions and sensory processing evaluated in hospital settings
options.D: Abilities that are psychological in nature and related to the practice of psychology

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-1(4) defines 'mental abilities' as abilities that are psychological in nature and related to the practice of psychology.

question_text: What degree is required for Georgia psychology licensure?

options.A: Doctoral degree from an APA/CPA accredited program in applied psychology (or equivalent)
options.B: Master's degree in clinical psychology from a regionally accredited institution plus three years of experience
options.C: Specialist in Education (Ed.S.) degree in school psychology with 1,500 hours of post-graduate internship
options.D: Doctoral degree in any behavioral science field regardless of program accreditation

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-8 and Rule 510-2-.04 require a doctoral degree from an APA/CPA accredited program in applied psychology (clinical, counseling, school, I/O) or an equivalent program meeting Board criteria.

question_text: How many years of qualifying experience are required by statute for licensure?

options.A: At least one year
options.B: At least two years
options.C: At least three years
options.D: At least four years

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-8 requires applicants to have at least two years of full-time qualifying supervised experience in psychology (internship plus postdoctoral SWE).

question_text: What happens if an applicant fails a board exam within the preceding six months?

options.A: The applicant is permanently barred from taking any future Georgia licensing examinations
options.B: The applicant may be granted a temporary practice permit under supervision
options.C: Ineligible for licensure at that time
options.D: The applicant is granted an automatic administrative waiver upon written petition

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-8 states that an applicant who has failed a board licensing examination within the preceding six months is ineligible for licensure at that time.

question_text: Is good moral character required for licensure?

options.A: No; licensure is determined solely by degree accreditation and examination passing scores
options.B: Only if the applicant has disclosed a prior criminal conviction or disciplinary action
options.C: No; good moral character evaluations were eliminated under administrative simplification rules
options.D: Yes; good moral character is a mandatory statutory prerequisite for licensure under OCGA 43-39-8

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-8 explicitly specifies good moral character as a mandatory statutory prerequisite for psychology licensure in Georgia.

question_text: What is the minimum postdoctoral supervised work experience hours required?

options.A: 1,500 hours
options.B: 1,750 hours
options.C: 1,000 hours
options.D: 2,000 hours

explanation: Rule 510-2-.05 requires a minimum of 1,500 hours of postdoctoral supervised work experience (SWE).

question_text: How long may the postdoctoral SWE extend?

options.A: No less than 6 months and no more than 12 months
options.B: No less than 11 months and no more than 24 months
options.C: No less than 12 months and no more than 36 months
options.D: No less than 18 months and no more than 30 months

explanation: Rule 510-2-.05 specifies that postdoctoral supervised work experience must be completed in no less than 11 months and no more than 24 months.

question_text: How many client/patient involvement hours must the SWE include?

options.A: Minimum 1,000 hours
options.B: Minimum 1,500 hours
options.C: Minimum 500 hours
options.D: Minimum 750 hours

explanation: Rule 510-2-.05 requires that the 1,500-hour postdoctoral SWE include a minimum of 500 hours of direct client/patient involvement.

question_text: What must the SWE weekly log contain?

options.A: Billing codes, client insurance records, and DSM-5 diagnostic formulations
options.B: Detailed psychotherapy process notes, treatment transcripts, and fee ledgers
options.C: Supervisor personal evaluations, audio recordings of sessions, and client outcome metrics
options.D: Activities, total hours, client/patient involvement hours, and individual supervision hours

explanation: Rule 510-2-.05 requires trainees to maintain a weekly log documenting activities, total hours, client/patient involvement hours, and individual supervision hours.

question_text: For licensure, what internship hours are required?

options.A: At least 2,000 hours
options.B: At least 1,750 hours
options.C: At least 1,500 hours
options.D: At least 2,500 hours

explanation: Rule 510-2-.05 requires a predoctoral internship of at least 2,000 hours completed within 11 to 24 months.

question_text: What is the minimum direct client contact hours for a clinical/counseling internship?

options.A: 1,000 hours (I/O interns exempt)
options.B: 500 hours (I/O interns exempt)
options.C: 1,500 hours (I/O interns exempt)
options.D: 750 hours (I/O interns exempt)

explanation: Rule 510-2-.05 requires at least 500 hours of direct client contact during the predoctoral internship for clinical and counseling interns; I/O interns are exempt from this direct contact requirement.

question_text: What percentage of internship supervision must be by licensed psychologists?

options.A: At least 50%
options.B: At least 65%
options.C: At least 80%

explanation: Rule 510-2-.05 mandates that at least 80% of internship supervision must be provided by licensed psychologists.

question_text: How many interns/fellows may a supervisor oversee concurrently without Board approval?

options.A: No more than two
options.B: No more than four
options.C: No more than five
options.D: No more than three

explanation: Rule 510-2-.05 and Rule 510-5-.06 restrict supervisors from supervising more than three interns, fellows, or psychological assistants concurrently without prior Board approval.

question_text: How long is a Georgia temporary psychology license valid?

options.A: 12 months from issuance; non-renewable
options.B: 6 months from issuance; renewable once
options.C: 24 months from issuance; non-renewable
options.D: 3 months from issuance; non-renewable

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-14 and Rule 510-9-.01 establish that a temporary license is valid for 12 months from issuance and is non-renewable.

question_text: How long is a Georgia provisional psychology license valid?

options.A: 18 months unless Board grants exception; non-renewable
options.B: 24 months unless Board grants exception; non-renewable
options.C: 12 months unless Board grants exception; non-renewable
options.D: 36 months unless Board grants exception; non-renewable

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-14 and Rule 510-9-.02 specify that a provisional license is valid for 24 months (unless an exception is granted by the Board) and is non-renewable.

question_text: What happens if a provisional license holder fails the oral exam?

options.A: The provisional license is immediately revoked with no opportunity for re-examination
options.B: The applicant must retake both the EPPP and the jurisprudence exam before oral re-examination
options.C: May take a second Full Board Exam after six months; a second failure means denial
options.D: The provisional license is automatically extended for 12 months without further examination

explanation: Rule 510-2-.01 provides that if a provisional license holder fails the oral exam, they may take a second Full Board Exam after a six-month waiting period; a second failure results in license denial.

question_text: How long is an inactive license valid?

options.A: Up to two years, after which the license automatically lapses and is canceled
options.B: Up to five years, provided the licensee completes 20 hours of continuing education annually
options.C: Exactly four years, during which the licensee may practice under supervision
options.D: Indefinite, but the licensee may not practice or use the title in Georgia

explanation: Rule 510-7-.03 provides that inactive license status is indefinite, but the individual may not practice psychology or use the title 'psychologist' in Georgia while inactive.

question_text: How frequently must Georgia psychology licenses be renewed?

options.A: Biennially
options.B: Annually
options.C: Triennially
options.D: Quadrennially

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-12 and Rule 510-7-.01 state that Georgia psychology licenses are renewed biennially (every two years).

question_text: When do Georgia psychology licenses expire?

options.A: June 30 of odd-numbered years
options.B: December 31 of even-numbered years
options.C: December 31 of odd-numbered years
options.D: June 30 of even-numbered years

explanation: Rule 510-7-.01 specifies that Georgia psychology licenses expire on December 31 of even-numbered years.

question_text: How many days after expiration may a license be renewed with a late fee?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 31 days
options.D: 90 days

explanation: Rule 510-7-.01 provides a late renewal period of 31 days (January 1 through January 31 following expiration) during which a license may be renewed with a penalty fee.

question_text: May a psychologist practice after December 31 of an even year before renewal?

options.A: Yes, during the 31-day late penalty period as long as a renewal application is pending
options.B: Yes, provided the psychologist practices exclusively in an exempt state or federal agency
options.C: Yes, for up to 90 days following expiration while continuing education audits are completed
options.D: No; license must be in active status

explanation: Rule 510-7-.01 provides that a psychologist may not practice after December 31 of an even year unless their license is active; practicing while expired constitutes unlicensed practice.

question_text: How many CE credits are required biennially for renewal?

options.A: 40 credits, including 6 in professional ethics
options.B: 30 credits, including 4 in professional ethics
options.C: 50 credits, including 10 in professional ethics
options.D: 20 credits, including 3 in professional ethics

explanation: Rule 510-8-.01 requires 40 continuing education credits per biennium, including a minimum of 6 credits in professional ethics.

question_text: How many ethics CE credits are required per biennium?

options.A: 3 credits, which may be satisfied via self-paced asynchronous reading
options.B: 6 credits, in-person or synchronous webinar
options.C: 10 credits, including at least 5 in Georgia mental health jurisprudence
options.D: 4 credits, earned through any APA-approved continuing education provider

explanation: Rule 510-8-.01 mandates that the 6 ethics CE credits must be earned through in-person workshops or live synchronous interactive webinars.

question_text: If licensed in the first year of the biennium, how many CE credits are required?

options.A: 40 credits, including 6 in professional ethics
options.B: 10 credits, with no specific ethics requirement
options.C: 20 credits, including 3 ethics
options.D: None; first-time licensees are fully exempt from the initial renewal cycle

explanation: Rule 510-8-.01 states that an individual licensed during the first year of the biennium must complete 20 CE credits, including 3 credits in ethics, for the initial renewal.

question_text: If licensed in the second year of the biennium, how many CE credits are required for first renewal?

options.A: 20 credits, including 3 ethics credits
options.B: 10 credits, with no ethics requirement
options.C: 6 credits in professional ethics only
options.D: No continuing education credits are required for the first renewal cycle

explanation: Rule 510-8-.01 provides that licensees licensed during the second year of the biennium are exempt from continuing education requirements for their first renewal.

question_text: How long must CE documentation be retained?

options.A: Four years
options.B: One year
options.C: Two years
options.D: Three years

explanation: Rule 510-8-.03 requires licensees to maintain documentation of completed continuing education activities for four years.

question_text: What happens if an audited licensee fails to document CE?

options.A: The license is immediately revoked with no cure period permitted
options.B: License will not be renewed; may obtain credits within 31 days
options.C: The licensee is placed on indefinite probationary status without fine
options.D: The licensee must re-take the EPPP examination within 6 months

explanation: Rule 510-8-.03 states that if an audited licensee fails to document CE, the license will not be renewed, but the licensee may obtain credits within 31 days (during late renewal).

question_text: How long after lapse may a Georgia psychology license be reinstated without re-examination?

options.A: Within two years
options.B: Within three years
options.C: Within one year
options.D: Within six months

explanation: Rule 510-7-.02 allows reinstatement of a lapsed license without re-examination if application is made within one year (12 months) of lapse.

question_text: What is required for reinstatement within one year of lapse?

options.A: Application, 40 CE hours within one year, and penalty fee
options.B: Application, 20 CE hours within two years, and penalty fee
options.C: Application, retaking the jurisprudence exam, and penalty fee
options.D: Application, 40 CE hours within two years, and penalty fee

explanation: Rule 510-7-.02 requires an application, documentation of 40 CE hours completed within the preceding two years, and payment of the penalty fee for reinstatement within one year of lapse.

question_text: What is required for reinstatement more than 12 months after lapse?

options.A: Application, 40 CE hours, plus passing Georgia Jurisprudence and Oral Examinations
options.B: Re-taking and passing all three licensure examinations: EPPP, Jurisprudence, and Oral
options.C: Submission of an application and payment of all accrued back renewal fees with no re-examination
options.D: Completion of 1,500 additional hours of postdoctoral supervised work experience

explanation: Rule 510-7-.02 specifies that reinstatement more than 12 months after lapse requires an application, 40 CE hours, and re-examination on both the Georgia Jurisprudence and Oral examinations.

question_text: Which of the following is a statutory ground for license revocation under OCGA 43-39-13?

options.A: Failure to join or maintain membership in the Georgia Psychological Association
options.B: Practicing under a false or assumed name
options.C: Refusing to provide pro bono psychological services to indigent clients annually
options.D: Charging fees exceeding standard Medicare or commercial insurance reimbursement rates

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-13 establishes statutory grounds for revocation or suspension, explicitly including practicing under a false or assumed name, fraud in applying for a license, felony conviction, habitual intemperance, and gross negligence.

question_text: What may the Board require if it believes a licensee is impaired?

options.A: Mandatory surrender of license within 48 hours without administrative hearing
options.B: Immediate referral to the county district attorney for criminal competency assessment
options.C: Mental/physical exam by Board-designated practitioner; production of records
options.D: Re-examination on the national EPPP examination within 30 days

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-13 empowers the Board to require an impaired licensee to submit to a mental or physical examination by a Board-designated practitioner and to produce medical records.

question_text: What may the Board do if a licensee refuses a directed impairment exam?

options.A: Fine the licensee up to $10,000 without further board action
options.B: Issue a public reprimand while allowing unrestricted practice to continue
options.C: Automatically convert the license to active emeritus status
options.D: Summarily suspend the license if public health/safety/welfare requires

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-13 authorizes the Board to summarily suspend a license if a licensee refuses a directed examination and public health, safety, or welfare requires emergency action.

question_text: Are impairment exam results privileged from board proceedings?

options.A: No; admissible despite any privilege claim
options.B: Yes; protected by the statutory psychologist-patient privilege under OCGA 43-39-16
options.C: Yes; admissible only if the licensee explicitly waives physician-patient confidentiality in writing
options.D: Yes; privileged unless a superior court judge issues an ex parte unsealing order

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-13 provides that results of Board-ordered impairment examinations are admissible in Board disciplinary proceedings notwithstanding any claim of privilege.

question_text: Within how many days must a licensee notify the Board of a felony conviction?

options.A: 14 days
options.B: 10 days
options.C: 15 days
options.D: 30 days

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-1-27 and O.C.G.A. § 16-13-111 require a licensee to notify the licensing board in writing within 10 days of any felony or drug conviction.

question_text: What is the minimum license suspension for a first controlled-substance/marijuana conviction?

options.A: Not less than one month
options.B: Not less than six months
options.C: Not less than three months
options.D: Not less than twelve months

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 16-13-111 provides that a first conviction for a controlled substance or marijuana offense results in a license suspension of not less than three months.

question_text: What happens to the license upon a second or subsequent drug conviction?

options.A: Mandatory suspension for a minimum of one year
options.B: Administrative probation with required random drug screening
options.C: Public reprimand and payment of a $1,000 civil fine
options.D: Mandatory revocation of the professional license

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 16-13-111 mandates that upon a second or subsequent drug conviction, the professional license must be revoked by operation of law.

question_text: What is the penalty for failure to notify the licensing authority of a drug conviction?

options.A: Grounds for revocation
options.B: A mandatory $500 civil fine with no license action
options.C: Automatic 30-day administrative suspension
options.D: Requirement to complete 10 additional ethics CE credits

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 16-13-111 specifies that failure of a licensed individual to notify the licensing authority of a conviction within 10 days is itself independent grounds for revocation.

question_text: When does the controlled-substance sanction article apply?

options.A: Offenses committed on or after January 1, 1980
options.B: Offenses committed on or after July 1, 1990
options.C: Offenses committed on or after July 1, 2000
options.D: Offenses committed on or after January 1, 2010

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 16-13-114 provides that Article 4 of Chapter 13 (licensed-person drug sanctions) applies to offenses committed on or after July 1, 1990.

question_text: For what crimes may a Georgia professional board deny/revoke a license?

options.A: Any misdemeanor traffic violation or infraction
options.B: Only federal civil rights violations adjudicated in federal court
options.C: Felony or crime involving moral turpitude
options.D: Non-violent misdemeanors not punishable by incarceration

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-1-19 authorizes professional licensing boards to discipline or revoke a license upon conviction of any felony or any crime involving moral turpitude.

question_text: Does a felony include out-of-state felonies for Georgia board purposes?

options.A: No; Georgia professional licensing boards have jurisdiction only over felonies committed within Georgia
options.B: Only if the out-of-state felony resulted in actual incarceration exceeding one year
options.C: Only if the other state's licensing board has already revoked the professional license
options.D: Yes, if the offense would be a felony in Georgia

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-1-19 provides that conviction of a felony in another state constitutes grounds for disciplinary action if the underlying acts would constitute a felony under Georgia law.

question_text: What disciplinary finding standard applies to the Georgia psychology board?

options.A: Majority of the entire board
options.B: Unanimous vote of all board members present
options.C: Two-thirds vote of a quorum of board members
options.D: Simple majority of board members present at the hearing

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-1-19 and Rule 510-6-.02 require a finding by a majority of the entire Board to impose disciplinary sanctions.

question_text: What sanctions may the Board impose?

options.A: Criminal misdemeanor incarceration up to 12 months in county jail
options.B: Refuse to grant/renew, suspend, revoke, discipline, or place on probation
options.C: Imposition of punitive damages payable directly to complaining clients
options.D: Issuance of permanent arrest warrants executed by the Division Director

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-1-19 and § 43-39-13 list authorized administrative sanctions: refuse to grant or renew, suspend, revoke, publicly or privately reprimand, or place on probation.

question_text: What must a psychologist report to the Board within 30 days?

options.A: Any change in office hourly fee schedules or accepted insurance networks
options.B: Initiation of an informal client fee dispute or refund negotiation
options.C: Sanctions/discipline by any lawful authority; voluntary surrender of any psychology license
options.D: The hiring of any new non-clinical administrative office personnel

explanation: Rule 510-5-.11 requires psychologists to report in writing within 30 days any disciplinary sanctions imposed by any lawful licensing authority or the voluntary surrender of any psychology license.

question_text: What privilege applies to psychologist-client communications in Georgia?

options.A: Physician-patient privilege under common law
options.B: Work-product doctrine applicable to civil litigation
options.C: Qualified peer review immunity under hospital regulations
options.D: Same as attorney-client privilege

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-16 provides that confidential communications between a licensed psychologist and client are placed upon the same basis as those provided by law between attorney and client.

question_text: Which Georgia evidence code section lists psychologist-patient privilege?
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 24-9-21(6) (and modern § 24-5-501(a)(6)) explicitly establishes the psychologist-patient privilege in the Georgia Evidence Code.

question_text: What other professionals' communications are privileged under OCGA 24-9-21?

options.A: Attorneys, clergy, and certified public accountants only
options.B: Psychiatrist-patient; licensed clinical social worker, clinical nurse specialist psych/mental health, marriage and family therapist, professional counselor during psychotherapeutic relationship
options.C: Physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech-language pathologists, and medical assistants
options.D: Registered nurses, hospital administrators, medical records clerks, and case managers

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 24-9-21 provides confidential communication privileges for psychiatrists, LCSWs, psychiatric CNSs, MFTs, and LPCs during psychotherapeutic relationships, on par with attorney-client and psychologist-patient privilege.

question_text: What is the misdemeanor penalty for unlicensed practice of psychology?

options.A: Fine $500-$5,000 and/or imprisonment up to 24 months
options.B: Fine $1,000-$5,000 and mandatory community service of 100 hours
options.C: Fine $100-$1,000 and/or imprisonment up to 12 months
options.D: Fine not to exceed $500 and no possibility of imprisonment

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-19 provides that any person practicing psychology without a valid license is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of $100 to $1,000, imprisonment up to 12 months, or both.

question_text: Who may bring an injunction for unlicensed practice?

options.A: The Georgia Psychological Association
options.B: Any aggrieved consumer or client
options.C: The Georgia Department of Public Health
options.D: The Board

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-18 provides that the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists may bring an action to enjoin any person from engaging in the unlicensed practice of psychology.

question_text: Must the Board prove no adequate remedy at law to get an injunction?

options.A: No; the Board is not required to show the lack of an adequate remedy at law to obtain an injunction
options.B: Yes, the Board must demonstrate irreparable harm and no adequate remedy at law
options.C: Yes, but only in petitions filed against non-resident corporate entities
options.D: Yes, unless the Attorney General certifies an immediate criminal emergency

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-18 and § 43-1-20 provide that the Board is not required to show that there is no adequate remedy at law to obtain an injunction against unlicensed practice.

question_text: Where is an unlicensed practice injunction filed?

options.A: Superior Court of Fulton County exclusively in all instances
options.B: County where the person resides or where corporation maintains principal office
options.C: The municipal court of the city where the unauthorized service occurred
options.D: The Georgia Court of Appeals by direct original petition

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-18 provides that an injunction action is filed in the superior court of the county where the person resides or where the corporation maintains its principal office.

question_text: May a business entity imply it practices psychology?

options.A: Yes, provided the corporate charter is registered with the Secretary of State as a professional corporation
options.B: Yes, if at least 51% of corporate stock is held by licensed healthcare providers of any discipline
options.C: Only if at least one employee/officer holds a current Georgia psychology license
options.D: No; business entities are strictly prohibited from offering psychological services under any circumstances

explanation: Rule 510-10-.02 provides that a firm, partnership, or corporation may not imply it renders psychological services unless at least one partner, officer, or employee holds a current Georgia psychology license.

question_text: What activities are exempt from licensure under OCGA 43-39-7?

options.A: Any master's-level therapist billing third-party insurance payers independently
options.B: Out-of-state psychologists providing permanent remote teletherapy to Georgia residents
options.C: Hospital pastoral counselors providing psychotropic medication management
options.D: School psychologists in accredited schools (no fees); teaching/research (no direct services); state employees pre-1996/1997; religious orgs; doctoral psychologists under licensed supervision

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-7 sets forth explicit statutory exemptions: school psychologists in accredited schools (without private fees), university teaching/research (without direct services), grandfathered state employees, religious practitioners, and supervised postdoctoral trainees.

question_text: May an unlicensed person supervise psychological services for training?

options.A: No; unlicensed individuals are strictly prohibited from supervising psychological services
options.B: Yes, provided the supervisor holds a master's degree in clinical mental health counseling
options.C: Yes, in institutional hospital settings accredited by the Joint Commission
options.D: Yes, if authorized by the training director and approved by an institutional review board

explanation: Rule 510-10-.01 strictly prohibits an unlicensed person from supervising psychological services for training or licensure purposes.

question_text: May an unlicensed person perform psychological services as an independent contractor for a licensed psychologist?

options.A: Yes, provided a formal 1099 independent contractor agreement is submitted to the Board
options.B: No; an unlicensed person may only deliver services as an employee under direct supervision, not as an independent contractor
options.C: Yes, provided the unlicensed person carries independent professional liability insurance
options.D: Yes, for up to 30 calendar days per calendar year under remote supervision

explanation: Rule 510-10-.01 prohibits an unlicensed person from rendering psychological services as an independent contractor for a licensed psychologist; psychological services by unlicensed staff may only be performed as a bona fide employee under direct supervision.

question_text: Who is immune from civil/criminal liability for good-faith board testimony or peer-review reports?

options.A: All citizens of Georgia regardless of profession or relationship to the proceedings
options.B: Unlicensed complainants and adverse parties in contested administrative hearings
options.C: Licensed psychologists who provide good-faith testimony or peer-review reports
options.D: Only state employees subpoenaed by the Division Director

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-20 provides immunity from civil or criminal liability to licensed psychologists who provide good-faith testimony to the Board or submit peer review reports.

question_text: Are supervising/monitoring psychologists liable to the monitored psychologist?

options.A: Yes, under vicarious liability and common law respondeat superior doctrine
options.B: Yes, if the monitored psychologist suffers economic loss from board action
options.C: Only if the supervising psychologist receives monetary compensation for supervision
options.D: No, if acting in good faith without fraud or malice

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-39-20 provides that a psychologist appointed by the Board to monitor or supervise another licensee is not liable to the monitored psychologist for acts performed in good faith without fraud or malice.

question_text: What is the licensure option for out-of-state licensees?

options.A: Licensure by endorsement
options.B: Licensure by automatic grandfathering
options.C: Licensure by reciprocal waiver without application
options.D: Licensure by provisional emergency declaration

explanation: Rule 510-3-.01 provides for licensure by endorsement for applicants licensed in other jurisdictions who meet Georgia statutory and rule equivalency standards.

question_text: How many years of licensure qualifies an applicant as a Senior Psychologist for endorsement?

options.A: 5 years
options.B: 10 years
options.C: 15 years
options.D: 20 years

explanation: Rule 510-3-.02 defines a 'Senior Psychologist' for endorsement as an applicant with at least 10 years of continuous active licensure in good standing in another jurisdiction.

question_text: What CPQ holders are deemed to meet Georgia licensure requirements?

options.A: ASPPB CPQ holders are granted immediate active Georgia licensure without examination
options.B: CPQ holders must complete 1,500 additional hours of postdoctoral Georgia supervision
options.C: ASPPB Certificate of Professional Qualification holders who pass jurisprudence and oral exams
options.D: CPQ holders must re-take and pass the national EPPP examination at the current pass point

explanation: Rule 510-3-.02 provides that holders of the ASPPB Certificate of Professional Qualification (CPQ) meet basic doctoral and experience requirements but must pass the Georgia Jurisprudence and Oral Examinations.

question_text: Who is a mandated reporter of child abuse in Georgia?

options.A: Only sworn law enforcement officers and hospital emergency physicians
options.B: Only school principals and public child welfare caseworkers
options.C: Only licensed physicians, dentists, and certified emergency medical technicians
options.D: Any person required under 19-7-5(c), including psychologists

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 19-7-5(c) lists mandated reporters of child abuse in Georgia, explicitly including psychologists, school psychologists, and other healthcare/mental health professionals.

question_text: What is 'child' under Georgia child abuse law?

options.A: Any person under 18 years of age
options.B: Any person under 16 years of age
options.C: Any person under 14 years of age
options.D: Any person under 21 years of age enrolled in secondary school

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 19-7-5 defines a 'child' as any person under 18 years of age.

question_text: What is 'child abuse' under Georgia law?

options.A: Reasonable corporal punishment administered by a parent or legal guardian
options.B: Physical injury or death inflicted by a parent/custodian/other caretaker
options.C: Normal childhood conflicts between siblings that cause emotional distress
options.D: Truancy or willful refusal to attend public school without parental consent

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 19-7-5 defines 'child abuse' as non-accidental physical injury, sexual abuse/exploitation, or severe neglect inflicted by a parent, guardian, or caretaker.

question_text: Who must report suspected abuse/neglect/exploitation of a disabled adult or elder person?

options.A: Only adult protective services caseworkers and nursing home directors
options.B: Only probate judges and designated county law enforcement officers
options.C: Mandated child abuse reporters, therapists, day-care personnel, coroners, EMS personnel, clergy, facility staff, financial institution employees, and any other person may report
options.D: Only hospital medical staff attending to physical injuries in an emergency department

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 30-5-4 specifies mandated reporters for abuse, neglect, or exploitation of disabled adults or elder persons, including child abuse reporters, mental health providers, medical staff, clergy, and facility personnel.

question_text: To whom must reports of disabled adult/elder abuse be made?

options.A: Exclusively to the Georgia composite medical board within 24 hours
options.B: The Department of Community Health and the Secretary of State
options.C: The Georgia State Board of Examiners of Psychologists
options.D: Adult protection agency and appropriate law enforcement or prosecuting attorney

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 30-5-4 requires reports of abuse, neglect, or exploitation of a disabled adult or elder person to be made to the Adult Protection Agency (DFCS/DAS) and appropriate law enforcement or prosecuting attorney.

question_text: Are reports of disabled adult/elder abuse immune from liability?

options.A: Yes, good-faith reporters are immune from civil/criminal liability
options.B: No; reporters may be sued for defamation if the investigation substantiates no abuse
options.C: Only if the reporter obtained an advance written opinion from legal counsel
options.D: Immune from civil damages only, but subject to criminal misdemeanor prosecution

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 30-5-4 provides that any person who in good faith makes a report of suspected elder or disabled adult abuse has immunity from any civil or criminal liability.

question_text: What is 'sexual contact' under OCGA 16-6-5.1?

options.A: Non-physical verbal comments or sexual innuendos delivered during a therapy session
options.B: Contact involving intimate parts of either person for sexual gratification
options.C: Any consensual social dating relationship established two years after termination
options.D: Standard physical touch involved in taking vital signs or neurological reflexes

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 16-6-5.1 defines 'sexual contact' as any contact involving the intimate parts of either person for the purpose of sexual gratification.

question_text: What is 'psychotherapy' under OCGA 16-6-5.1?

options.A: Academic instruction and tutoring in psychology delivered in university settings
options.B: General life coaching and organizational consulting for corporate executives
options.C: Professional treatment or counseling of a mental or emotional illness, symptom, or condition
options.D: Career counseling and vocational interest inventory administration

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 16-6-5.1 defines 'psychotherapy' as the professional treatment, assessment, or counseling of a mental or emotional illness, symptom, or condition.

question_text: What are 'intimate parts' under OCGA 16-6-5.1?

options.A: Hands, wrists, forearms, shoulders, and neck
options.B: Face, hair, ears, and temples
options.C: Feet, ankles, and lower legs below the knee
options.D: Genital area, groin, inner thighs, buttocks, or breasts

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 16-6-5.1 defines 'intimate parts' as the genital area, groin, inner thighs, buttocks, or breasts.

question_text: What is a 'health service provider psychologist'?

options.A: Licensed psychologist meeting training/experience criteria who delivers direct preventive, assessment, and therapeutic services to impaired or at-risk individuals
options.B: Any licensed psychologist who maintains active commercial insurance panel contracts
options.C: A psychologist employed exclusively as a hospital chief executive officer or administrator
options.D: A researcher conducting clinical psychopharmacology trials in an academic medical center

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 31-7-160 defines a 'health service provider psychologist' as a licensed psychologist meeting training and experience standards who provides direct preventive, assessment, or therapeutic services to impaired or at-risk individuals.

question_text: What is a 'psychologist's order'?

options.A: A prescription for Schedule II controlled psychotropic substances
options.B: Order by a health service provider psychologist for care/treatment in a medical facility, excluding meds, nursing assessments, or medical procedures
options.C: A judicial mandate issued by a superior court ordering psychiatric commitment
options.D: A directive instructing registered nurses to perform surgical diagnostic procedures

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 31-7-160 defines a 'psychologist's order' as an order for care, treatment, or diagnostic assessment in a medical facility, expressly excluding medication orders, nursing assessments, or invasive medical procedures.

question_text: How many hours of supervised health-service experience are required?

options.A: Not less than one year, 1,000 hours total
options.B: Not less than three years, 2,000 hours each year
options.C: Not less than two years, 1,500 hours each year
options.D: Not less than four years, 1,200 hours each year

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 31-7-162 requires an applicant for health service provider status to have not less than two years of full-time supervised experience in health service psychology (at least 1,500 hours each year).

question_text: How many supportive recommendation letters are required for health service provider status?

options.A: One letter from an APA-accredited doctoral program director
options.B: Three letters from licensed psychiatrists with active hospital admitting privileges
options.C: Four letters from members of the Georgia State Board of Examiners
options.D: Two from health service providers in psychology

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 31-7-162 requires two supportive letters of recommendation from health service providers in psychology.

question_text: Must health service provider experience include inpatient work?

options.A: A substantial portion must be in an inpatient setting
options.B: No; all experience may be completed in private outpatient independent practice
options.C: Only if the psychologist intends to prescribe psychoactive medications
options.D: Inpatient work is strictly prohibited during predoctoral and postdoctoral training

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 31-7-162 requires that a substantial portion of the qualifying health-service experience be completed in an inpatient facility setting.

question_text: Who must be designated responsible for medical aspects of a patient admitted by a psychologist?

options.A: The hospital risk management officer
options.B: A physician
options.C: The clinical nurse specialist
options.D: The supervising psychologist

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 31-7-161 requires that when a patient is admitted by a psychologist to a healthcare facility, a physician must be designated as responsible for all medical aspects of the patient's care.

question_text: May an RN or LPN execute a psychologist's order?

options.A: No; nurses may only execute orders issued directly by licensed physicians
options.B: Only after obtaining secondary written approval from the hospital ethics board
options.C: Yes; they may confer with the psychologist
options.D: Only in designated psychiatric emergency departments during night shifts

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 31-7-161 authorizes registered nurses and licensed practical nurses to execute psychologist orders within their scope of practice, conferring with the psychologist as needed.

question_text: What action is required when a health facility denies or revokes health service provider staff privileges?

options.A: Within 180 days to the American Psychological Association Ethics Committee
options.B: Within 60 days to the county medical society and district attorney
options.C: Privileges actions are internal hospital matters and need not be reported
options.D: Reported by the facility to the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 31-7-165 requires medical facilities to report the denial, restriction, or revocation of health service provider staff privileges to the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists.

question_text: Within how many hours must a physician have personally examined a person before executing an involuntary-treatment certificate?

options.A: 48 hours
options.B: 24 hours
options.C: 72 hours
options.D: 12 hours

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 37-3-41 requires that a physician personally examine the individual within the 48 hours immediately preceding the execution of an involuntary admission certificate.

question_text: How long is a physician's involuntary-treatment certificate valid?

options.A: 48 hours after execution
options.B: Seven days after execution
options.C: 14 days after execution
options.D: 30 days after execution

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 37-3-41 provides that a physician's involuntary admission certificate expires seven days after its date of execution.

question_text: Within how many hours must a peace officer act after receiving a physician's certificate?

options.A: 48 hours
options.B: 96 hours
options.C: 72 hours
options.D: 24 hours

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 37-3-41 requires a peace officer who receives a physician's certificate to take the person into custody within 72 hours.

question_text: How many affiants are required for a court order for involuntary examination if no unexpired physician certificate?

options.A: At least one person
options.B: At least three persons
options.C: At least four persons
options.D: At least two persons

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 37-3-41 provides that a court order for involuntary examination without a physician certificate requires affidavits from at least two persons.

question_text: Within how many hours must affiants have seen the person for a court order?

options.A: 48 hours
options.B: 24 hours
options.C: 72 hours
options.D: 12 hours

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 37-3-41 requires that the affiants for a court order have personally observed the individual within the preceding 48 hours.

question_text: How long is a court order for involuntary examination valid?

options.A: 48 hours after issuance
options.B: Seven days after issuance
options.C: 14 days after issuance
options.D: 30 days after issuance

explanation: O.C.G.A. § 37-3-41 specifies that a court order for involuntary examination expires seven days after its date of issuance.

question_text: What must psychologists do if they learn of misuse of their work?

options.A: Immediately file a civil tort suit for intellectual property infringement
options.B: Report the misuser to local criminal law enforcement authorities within 24 hours
options.C: Take reasonable steps to correct or minimize misuse/misrepresentation
options.D: Resign immediately from all professional associations and academic positions

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 1.01 (adopted in Rule 510-4-.02) requires psychologists who learn of misuse or misrepresentation of their work to take reasonable steps to correct or minimize it.

question_text: What should psychologists do when ethics conflict with law?

options.A: Ethics always supersede law; disobey the law regardless of legal consequence
options.B: Immediately file an emergency constitutional injunction in federal district court
options.C: Disregard ethical standards entirely without acknowledging the ethical commitment
options.D: Make known commitment to Ethics Code and attempt to resolve; if unresolvable, may follow law

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 1.02 (Rule 510-4-.02) directs psychologists whose ethical responsibilities conflict with law to make known their commitment to the Ethics Code and take steps to resolve the conflict; if unresolvable, they may adhere to the requirements of the law.

question_text: When must psychologists report ethical violations?

options.A: When substantial harm has occurred or is likely and informal resolution is inappropriate or fails
options.B: For any technical ethics violation regardless of severity, harm, or confidentiality
options.C: Only after a formal criminal indictment has been returned by a grand jury
options.D: Never; psychologists have no affirmative obligation to report colleague misconduct

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 1.05 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires formal reporting of ethical violations when an apparent violation has substantially harmed or is likely to substantially harm a person and informal resolution is not appropriate or fails.

question_text: Is failure to cooperate with an ethics investigation itself a violation?

options.A: No; licensees may invoke Fifth Amendment rights in administrative proceedings without ethics consequences
options.B: Yes; failure to cooperate with a lawful Board investigation constitutes an independent disciplinary violation
options.C: No; cooperation is entirely voluntary under APA and Georgia Board procedural rules
options.D: Only if the investigation involves felony criminal charges or patient sexual abuse

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 1.06 and Rule 510-5-.10 provide that failure to cooperate with an ethics investigation or Board inquiry is itself an independent ethical and regulatory violation.

question_text: What is the basis for the boundaries of psychologists' competence?

options.A: Personal lived experience and subjective self-assessment of capability
options.B: Completion of any undergraduate psychology degree program
options.C: Education, training, supervised experience, consultation, study, or professional experience
options.D: Possession of a general state business license and malpractice insurance

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 2.01 (Rule 510-4-.02) specifies that psychologists provide services within the boundaries of their competence based on education, training, supervised experience, consultation, study, or professional experience.

question_text: When may psychologists provide services in an emergency without prior competence?

options.A: At any time, provided the psychologist charges discounted pro bono fee rates
options.B: Only if a licensed physician is physically present in the treatment room
options.C: Under no circumstances; practicing outside competence is strictly prohibited even in emergencies
options.D: When other mental health services are unavailable and they make reasonable efforts to obtain competence

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 2.02 (Rule 510-4-.02) allows psychologists to provide emergency services for which they lack full competence when other services are unavailable, provided they discontinue services as soon as the emergency ends or appropriate services become available.

question_text: Must psychologists maintain competence?

options.A: Yes; undertake ongoing efforts
options.B: No; competence is permanently established upon initial doctoral graduation and licensure
options.C: Only if required by an employer or health insurance managed care organization
options.D: Only during the first five years of independent clinical practice

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 2.03 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires psychologists to undertake ongoing efforts to develop and maintain their professional competence.

question_text: What must psychologists ensure when delegating work?

options.A: Delegatees must carry independent professional liability insurance policies
options.B: Persons are competent, have no exploitative multiple relationship, and perform competently
options.C: Delegatees must be licensed independent practitioners in another health field
options.D: Delegation is permitted only to tenured university faculty or hospital staff

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 2.05 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires psychologists delegating work to avoid delegating to persons with multiple relationships and to authorize only services they are competent to perform.

question_text: On what bases may psychologists not discriminate?

options.A: Solely on the basis of a client's ability to pay out-of-pocket private cash rates
options.B: Client clinical diagnosis or DSM-5 diagnostic category
options.C: Age, gender, gender identity, race, ethnicity, culture, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, disability, socioeconomic status, or any basis proscribed by law
options.D: Geographic county of residence or distance from the psychologist's office

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 3.01 (Rule 510-4-.02) prohibits unfair discrimination based on age, gender, gender identity, race, ethnicity, culture, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, disability, socioeconomic status, or any basis proscribed by law.

question_text: When should psychologists avoid a multiple relationship?

options.A: Any time a client and psychologist share any common acquaintance or social club
options.B: Only when the client expressly objects in writing to the dual relationship
options.C: Whenever a psychologist accepts a holiday gift valued under twenty-five dollars
options.D: When it could impair objectivity, competence, or effectiveness, or risk exploitation or harm

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 3.05 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires psychologists to refrain from entering multiple relationships that could reasonably be expected to impair objectivity, competence, or effectiveness, or cause exploitation or harm.

question_text: What must psychologists clarify at the outset of third-party-requested services?

options.A: The specific billing codes to be submitted to commercial health insurance
options.B: The identity of all expert witnesses who may testify in subsequent litigation
options.C: Role, who is the client, probable uses of information, and limits of confidentiality
options.D: The complete psychometric test battery to be administered during assessment

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 3.07 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires psychologists providing third-party-requested services to clarify at the outset the nature of the relationship, who the client is, probable uses of findings, and limits of confidentiality.

question_text: What must informed consent include?

options.A: Guarantees of complete symptom cure and successful therapeutic outcome
options.B: An irrevocable waiver of the client's right to file board ethics complaints
options.C: Mandatory agreement to participate in ongoing academic research studies
options.D: Nature/procedures, risks/benefits, limits of confidentiality, fees, third parties, opportunity to ask questions

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 3.10 and 10.01 (Rule 510-4-.02) mandate that informed consent cover the nature and anticipated course of services, risks/benefits, fees, involvement of third parties, limits of confidentiality, and opportunity to ask questions.

question_text: What must psychologists plan for when interrupting psychological services?

options.A: Transferring all active clinical files to the local county courthouse for storage
options.B: Facilitating services in event of illness, death, unavailability, relocation, or financial limitations
options.C: Immediately refunding all historical fees collected throughout the entire treatment course
options.D: Automatically terminating all clients without notice upon reaching age sixty-five

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 3.12 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires psychologists to make reasonable efforts to facilitate service continuation in the event psychological services are interrupted by factors such as illness, death, unavailability, relocation, or financial limitations.

question_text: What is psychologists' primary obligation regarding confidentiality?

options.A: Absolute confidentiality with zero exceptions under any circumstances
options.B: Maintaining confidentiality only until the client terminates active therapy
options.C: Disclosing client information upon informal request by law enforcement officers
options.D: Take reasonable precautions to protect confidential information

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 4.01 (Rule 510-4-.02) provides that psychologists have a primary obligation and must take reasonable precautions to protect confidential information.

question_text: When must psychologists discuss limits of confidentiality?

options.A: At the outset of the relationship and thereafter as circumstances warrant
options.B: Only after a breach of confidentiality or legal subpoena has actually occurred
options.C: Exclusively at the termination session when closing the clinical chart
options.D: Only if the client explicitly inquires about confidentiality policies

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 4.02 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires psychologists to discuss the relevant limits of confidentiality at the outset of the relationship and thereafter as new circumstances warrant.

question_text: When may psychologists record voices/images of clients?

options.A: At any time without notice if used solely for educational purposes
options.B: After obtaining permission
options.C: Only when authorized by an ex parte judicial wiretap warrant
options.D: Whenever conducting court-ordered forensic child custody evaluations

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 4.03 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires psychologists to obtain permission from clients or their legal representatives prior to recording voices or images.

question_text: What standard governs disclosures of confidential information without consent?

options.A: Psychologists may disclose confidential information whenever requested by family members
options.B: Disclosures without consent are strictly prohibited under every statutory provision
options.C: Only as mandated by law or permitted by law for valid purposes, limited to the minimum necessary
options.D: Disclosures are permitted whenever advantageous to the psychologist's academic research

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 4.05 (Rule 510-4-.02) permits disclosures without consent only as mandated by law or permitted by law for a valid purpose, disclosing only the minimum necessary information.

question_text: What must psychologists do before consulting about a client?

options.A: Obtain a notarized release signed by the client and both of the client's parents
options.B: Disclose the client's full legal name, social security number, and home address
options.C: Conduct the consultation exclusively in public professional peer review meetings
options.D: Not disclose identifying information unless consent obtained or unavoidable, and limit to necessary extent

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 4.06 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires that when consulting with colleagues, psychologists do not disclose confidential identifying information without prior consent and disclose information only to the extent necessary.

question_text: What must paid advertisements by psychologists be?

options.A: Identified or clearly recognizable as paid advertisements
options.B: Pre-approved by the Georgia State Board of Examiners prior to publication
options.C: Accompanied by full disclosure of all client fees and billing dispute policies
options.D: Published exclusively in peer-reviewed scientific psychology journals

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 5.02(c) (Rule 510-4-.02) provides that paid advertisements regarding psychologists' services must be identified or clearly recognizable as such.

question_text: From whom may psychologists not solicit testimonials?

options.A: Professional colleagues who have attended the psychologist's CE workshops
options.B: Current therapy clients/patients or vulnerable persons
options.C: Former academic professors from the psychologist's doctoral training program
options.D: Community leaders and local public officials who know the psychologist's character

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 5.05 (Rule 510-4-.02) prohibits psychologists from soliciting testimonials from current therapy clients or other persons who because of particular circumstances are vulnerable to undue influence.

question_text: May psychologists engage in uninvited in-person solicitation of therapy clients?

options.A: Yes; in-person solicitation is protected commercial speech under the First Amendment
options.B: Yes, provided the psychologist offers free initial diagnostic consultations
options.C: No, except for collateral contacts or disaster/community outreach
options.D: Yes, in hospital waiting rooms and emergency departments

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 5.06 (Rule 510-4-.02) prohibits uninvited in-person solicitation of business from actual or potential therapy clients, except for collateral contacts to implement therapy or disaster/community outreach.

question_text: May psychologists withhold records solely because payment has not been received?

options.A: Yes; psychologists retain an absolute common-law artisan lien on all records until paid
options.B: Yes, provided the outstanding fee balance has been formally referred to a collection agency
options.C: Yes, except when the client is involved in active bankruptcy proceedings
options.D: No, not records needed for emergency treatment

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 6.03 (Rule 510-4-.02) explicitly provides that psychologists may not withhold records under their control that are requested and needed for a client's emergency treatment solely because payment has not been received.

question_text: What must fee agreements specify?

options.A: Compensation and billing arrangements as early as feasible
options.B: Fixed sliding scale fees determined exclusively by federal poverty guidelines
options.C: Guarantees that fees will never increase throughout the lifetime of the client
options.D: Mandatory pre-payment for all therapy sessions six months in advance

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 6.04 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires that as early as feasible in a professional or scientific relationship, psychologists and recipients reach an agreement specifying compensation and billing arrangements.

question_text: May psychologists barter with clients?

options.A: Bartering is strictly prohibited under all circumstances in Georgia psychology
options.B: Only if not clinically contraindicated and not exploitative
options.C: Yes, provided bartered services are exchanged at 50% fair market cash value
options.D: Yes, but only for tangible goods and never for personal or professional services

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 6.05 (Rule 510-4-.02) permits bartering with clients only if it is not clinically contraindicated and the resulting arrangement is not exploitative.

question_text: What must reports to payers accurately reflect?

options.A: Any billing code that maximizes insurance reimbursement for the client
options.B: Generalized medical codes that conceal mental health diagnoses
options.C: Nature of service, fees, provider identity, findings, diagnosis
options.D: Detailed psychotherapy process transcripts and client personal diary entries

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 6.06 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires reports to payers to accurately state the nature of the service provided, fees, identity of the provider, findings, and diagnosis.

question_text: May psychologists require students to disclose personal sexual history?

options.A: Yes; complete personal disclosure is mandatory in all accredited clinical psychology programs
options.B: Yes, provided the disclosure occurs during group supervision sessions
options.C: Yes, whenever faculty members believe it will enhance clinical empathy
options.D: No, except if required in admissions materials or necessary to evaluate impairment

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 7.04 (Rule 510-4-.02) prohibits requiring students to disclose personal sexual history unless clearly identified in program admissions materials or necessary to evaluate an impaired student.

question_text: May faculty who evaluate students also provide required therapy to those students?

options.A: No; faculty who evaluate academic performance may not personally provide required therapy to those students
options.B: Yes, provided the faculty member does not assign grades in clinical practicum courses
options.C: Yes, if the student signs an informed consent waiving evaluative conflicts
options.D: Yes, whenever outside therapy resources are unavailable within a 50-mile radius

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 7.05 (Rule 510-4-.02) prohibits faculty who are responsible for evaluating students' academic performance from personally providing mandatory psychotherapy to those students.

question_text: May psychologists have sexual relationships with students/supervisees over whom they have evaluative authority?

options.A: Yes, provided the relationship is consensual and disclosed to the department chair
options.B: No; psychologists may not engage in sexual relationships with students or supervisees over whom they hold evaluative authority
options.C: Yes, after a mandatory waiting period of six months from course enrollment
options.D: Yes, if both parties sign an institutional conflict-of-interest waiver

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 7.07 (Rule 510-4-.02) strictly prohibits psychologists from engaging in sexual relationships with students or supervisees who are in their department, agency, or training center or over whom they have evaluative authority.

question_text: When may psychologists dispense with informed consent for research?

options.A: In any research study funded by state or federal research grants
options.B: Whenever obtaining consent would reduce the statistical power of the sample
options.C: Only in specified low-risk settings or where permitted by law
options.D: Psychologists may never dispense with informed consent in any research setting

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 8.05 (Rule 510-4-.02) permits dispensing with informed consent only where research would not reasonably be expected to create distress or harm (e.g. normal educational practices, anonymous questionnaires, naturalistic observation) or where permitted by law.

question_text: When is deception in research prohibited?

options.A: Whenever the research study involves undergraduate college students
options.B: When the study investigates social psychology or cognitive heuristics
options.C: Whenever research results will be published in peer-reviewed journals
options.D: When expected to cause physical pain or severe emotional distress

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 8.07 (Rule 510-4-.02) explicitly forbids deception in research that is reasonably expected to cause physical pain or severe emotional distress.

question_text: What must psychologists do after using deception in research?

options.A: Explain deception as early as feasible and allow withdrawal of data
options.B: Maintain deception indefinitely to prevent contamination of future study cohorts
options.C: Notify the institutional review board within 24 hours of each debriefing session
options.D: Pay each participant double the standard monetary research compensation

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 8.07 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires psychologists to explain any deception as early as feasible (preferably at conclusion of participation, but no later than data collection conclusion) and permit participants to withdraw their data.

question_text: What is the plagiarism rule?

options.A: Presenting another's work is permitted if paraphrased without citation
options.B: Do not present another's work or data as one's own, even if cited
options.C: Plagiarism rules apply only to published books and not journal articles or dissertations
options.D: Borrowing up to 25% of another's text without attribution is considered fair use

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 8.11 (Rule 510-4-.02) provides that psychologists do not present portions of another's work or data as their own, even if the other work or data source is cited occasionally.

question_text: Who should be principal author on a dissertation-based article?

options.A: The department chairperson who secured grant funding for the laboratory
options.B: The dissertation faculty advisor who supervised the research design
options.C: The student, except under exceptional circumstances
options.D: Authorship must always be listed strictly alphabetically regardless of contribution

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 8.12 (Rule 510-4-.02) provides that except under exceptional circumstances, a student is listed as principal author on any multiple-authored article substantially based on the student's doctoral dissertation.

question_text: What must psychologists base assessment opinions on?

options.A: Intuitive clinical impressions gathered during an informal initial meeting
options.B: Testimonials and collateral reports from interested third-party family members
options.C: Information and techniques sufficient to substantiate findings
options.D: Statistical averages of the demographic group without individualized testing

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 9.01 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires psychologists to base opinions contained in recommendations, reports, and evaluative statements on information and techniques sufficient to substantiate their findings.

question_text: What is 'test data' under the APA Ethics Code?

options.A: Raw and scaled scores, client responses, and psychologist notes/recordings during examination
options.B: Published psychometric test manuals, test protocols, stimuli, and test questions
options.C: Peer-reviewed validation studies evaluating norm samples and reliability coefficients
options.D: Billing codes, clinical appointment logs, and fee payment receipts

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 9.04 (Rule 510-4-.02) defines 'test data' as raw and scaled scores, client/patient responses to test questions or stimuli, and psychologists' notes and recordings concerning client statements and behavior during examination.

question_text: To whom may test data be released without a client release?

options.A: Any family member who pays for the psychological evaluation
options.B: The client's employer upon submission of a formal workplace inquiry
options.C: Only as required by law or court order
options.D: Any licensed healthcare professional requesting records by telephone

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 9.04 (Rule 510-4-.02) provides that in the absence of a client/patient release, psychologists provide test data only as required by law or court order.

question_text: What must assessment instruments have for the population tested?

options.A: Established validity and reliability; if not, describe limitations
options.B: Formal endorsement and certification by the Georgia Department of Education
options.C: Public-domain status allowing unrestricted photocopying of test stimuli
options.D: Universal cultural applicability without need for normative adaptations

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 9.02 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires assessment instruments to have established validity and reliability for the population tested; when validity/reliability is not established, psychologists describe strengths and limitations of test results.

question_text: May psychologists base decisions on obsolete or outdated test results?

options.A: Yes, if the older test version is less expensive for the client to purchase
options.B: No; psychologists do not base assessment decisions or recommendations on outdated tests or obsolete test data
options.C: Yes, provided the psychologist notes that the test was published within the past 25 years
options.D: Yes, in forensic evaluations where historical baselines are unavailable

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 9.08 (Rule 510-4-.02) prohibits psychologists from basing assessment decisions, interventions, or recommendations on outdated tests or obsolete test data.

question_text: What does 'test materials' include?

options.A: Manuals, instruments, protocols, and test questions/stimuli; excludes test data
options.B: Raw and scaled scores, client test answer sheets, and clinical interview notes
options.C: Psychotherapy process notes and audio recordings of clinical intake sessions
options.D: Billing statements, superbills, and insurance explanation of benefits forms

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 9.11 (Rule 510-4-.02) defines 'test materials' as manuals, instruments, protocols, and test questions or stimuli, explicitly excluding test data as defined in Standard 9.04.

question_text: What is psychologists' responsibility regarding test security?

options.A: Test questions and protocols should be made available online for public transparency
options.B: Release test manuals and test protocols to attorneys upon receipt of a standard civil subpoena
options.C: Make reasonable efforts to maintain integrity and security consistent with law
options.D: Discard all test protocols immediately after scoring to prevent third-party access

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 9.11 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires psychologists to make reasonable efforts to maintain the integrity and security of test materials consistent with law and contractual obligations.

question_text: May psychologists promote assessment use by unqualified persons?

options.A: Yes, whenever unqualified persons purchase automated computer scoring software
options.B: Yes, to reduce clinical assessment backlogs in public community clinics
options.C: Yes, provided the unqualified person charges reduced administrative fees
options.D: No, except for training with appropriate supervision

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 9.07 (Rule 510-4-.02) prohibits psychologists from promoting the use of psychological assessment techniques by unqualified persons, except when conducted for training purposes with appropriate supervision.

question_text: Must explanations of assessment results be provided?

options.A: Explanations are discretionary and psychologists may refuse to explain results at will
options.B: Only if the examinee pays an additional separate consultation fee for explanation
options.C: Never in forensic, pre-employment, or security screening evaluations
options.D: Yes, unless the relationship precludes it and this was explained in advance

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 9.10 (Rule 510-4-.02) requires psychologists to take reasonable steps to ensure that explanations of results are given, unless the nature of the relationship precludes providing an explanation (e.g. employment screening) and this was clearly explained to the person in advance.

question_text: What information must be included in informed consent to therapy?

options.A: Nature/anticipated course of therapy, fees, third parties, limits of confidentiality
options.B: Absolute guarantees of complete cure and permanent relief from symptoms
options.C: An agreement that the client will not consult other healthcare professionals
options.D: Detailed resumes and personal background disclosures of the psychologist
