explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 10.01 (Rule 510-4-.02) mandates that informed consent to therapy inform clients about the nature and anticipated course of therapy, fees, involvement of third parties, and limits of confidentiality.

question_text: May psychologists engage in sexual intimacies with current therapy clients?

options.A: Yes, if both parties give written informed consent
options.B: No; psychologists are strictly prohibited from engaging in sexual intimacies with current therapy clients
options.C: Yes, provided therapy is conducted in an outpatient community setting
options.D: Yes, if the client initiates the sexual intimacy

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 10.05 and Rule 510-5-.03 strictly prohibit psychologists from engaging in sexual intimacies with current therapy clients/patients.

question_text: May psychologists have sexual intimacies with close relatives/significant others of current clients?

options.A: Yes, because relatives are not direct clients of the psychologist
options.B: Yes, provided the client gives written permission
options.C: No; psychologists may not engage in sexual intimacies with individuals known to be close relatives or significant others of current clients
options.D: Yes, if the relative resides in a different household from the client

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 10.06 (Rule 510-4-.02) strictly prohibits sexual intimacies with individuals known to be close relatives, guardians, or significant others of current clients/patients.

question_text: May psychologists accept as clients persons with whom they had prior sexual intimacies?

options.A: Yes, if at least two years have elapsed since the prior sexual relationship
options.B: Yes, provided another psychologist conducts concurrent supervision
options.C: Yes, in emergency crisis situations where other providers are unavailable
options.D: No; psychologists do not accept as therapy clients persons with whom they have engaged in sexual intimacies

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 10.07 (Rule 510-4-.02) states that psychologists do not accept as therapy clients/patients persons with whom they have engaged in sexual intimacies.

question_text: For how long after termination are sexual intimacies with former clients prohibited?

options.A: At least two years
options.B: At least one year
options.C: At least five years
options.D: At least six months

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 10.08 (Rule 510-4-.02) prohibits sexual intimacies with former clients/patients for at least two years after cessation or termination of therapy.

question_text: After two years, who bears the burden of showing no exploitation with a former client sexual relationship?

options.A: The former client who alleges exploitation
options.B: The psychologist
options.C: The Georgia State Board of Examiners
options.D: The American Psychological Association Ethics Committee

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 10.08 (Rule 510-4-.02) explicitly places the burden on the psychologist to demonstrate that there has been no exploitation, in light of all relevant factors.

question_text: When should psychologists terminate therapy?

options.A: Exclusively when the client exhausts private health insurance benefits
options.B: Whenever the client expresses disagreement with the psychologist's personal beliefs
options.C: When no longer needed, not likely to benefit, or being harmed; also if threatened
options.D: Only when the psychologist retires or relocates to another state

explanation: APA Ethics Code Standard 10.10 (Rule 510-4-.02) directs psychologists to terminate therapy when it becomes reasonably clear that the client no longer needs the service, is not likely to benefit, or is being harmed, and permits termination if threatened or endangered by the client.

question_text: What chapters constitute the Georgia psychology Code of Ethics and Supplemental Code of Conduct?

options.A: Chapters 510-1 and 510-2
options.B: Chapters 510-2 and 510-3
options.C: Chapters 510-6 and 510-7
options.D: Chapters 510-4 and 510-5

explanation: Rule 510-5-.01 establishes that Chapter 510-4 (Code of Ethics) and Chapter 510-5 (Supplemental Code of Conduct) constitute the ethical standards and rules of conduct for Georgia psychologists.

question_text: Do the Georgia codes apply to applicants and students?

options.A: Yes; they apply to all licensees and applicants, including conduct during required education/training/employment
options.B: No; the codes apply strictly to fully licensed psychologists holding active licenses
options.C: No; students and applicants are governed solely by university honor codes
options.D: Only to postdoctoral fellows who have completed doctoral degrees

explanation: Rule 510-5-.01 provides that the Georgia Code of Ethics and Code of Conduct apply to all licensees and applicants for licensure, including conduct during education, training, and employment required for licensure.

question_text: Who is the client when a corporation is the contracting party?

options.A: Every individual employee of the corporation who participates in services
options.B: The organization, unless a separate professional relationship with an individual exists
options.C: The individual CEO or president of the contracting corporation
options.D: The Georgia Department of Labor

explanation: Rule 510-5-.02 provides that when a corporation or organizational entity is the contracting party, the organization is the client, unless a separate professional relationship with an individual employee is formally established.

question_text: What is 'telepsychology' in Georgia rules?

options.A: The automated computerized scoring of personality assessment instruments
options.B: The broadcasting of educational mental health lectures on public television
options.C: Provision of psychological services using telecommunication technologies
options.D: The electronic billing and filing of healthcare insurance claims

explanation: Rule 510-5-.02 defines 'telepsychology' as the provision of psychological services using telecommunication technologies (e.g. video conferencing, telephone, secure electronic communication).

question_text: What is required to practice telepsychology in Georgia?

options.A: A national telebehavioral health certificate with no state license
options.B: A valid license in any U.S. state without notification or PSYPACT authority
options.C: Registration with the Federal Communications Commission (FCC)
options.D: Current active Georgia license or PSYPACT authorization

explanation: Rule 510-5-.07 requires any individual practicing telepsychology with clients located in Georgia to possess a current, active Georgia psychology license or valid PSYPACT authorization to practice interjurisdictional telepsychology (APIT).

question_text: Must telepsychology meet the same standards as in-person services?

options.A: Yes; telepsychology services must adhere to the same professional standards, ethics, and rules as in-person practice
options.B: No; telepsychology is exempt from state confidentiality and informed consent rules
options.C: No; telepsychology is subject to relaxed standards of documentation and recordkeeping
options.D: Only when providing services to minors under 18 years of age

explanation: Rule 510-5-.07 specifies that telepsychology services must adhere to the exact same legal, ethical, and clinical practice standards as in-person psychological practice in Georgia.

question_text: What PSYPACT credentials allow interjurisdictional telepsychology?

options.A: ASPPB Interjurisdictional Practice Certificate (IPC) and TAP authorization
options.B: ASPPB E.Passport and APIT authorization
options.C: Certificate of Professional Qualification (CPQ) and Georgia temporary license
options.D: ABPP Specialty Diploma and National Register Health Service Psychologist credential

explanation: Rule 510-5-.07 and PSYPACT rules establish that interjurisdictional telepsychology requires an ASPPB E.Passport and Authority to Practice Interjurisdictional Telepsychology (APIT).

question_text: How often must IPC and TAP be renewed under PSYPACT?

options.A: Biennially (every two years)
options.B: Every three years
options.C: Annually
options.D: Every five years

explanation: Rule 510-9-.03 and PSYPACT regulations require ASPPB credentials (IPC, E.Passport) and PSYPACT authorities (TAP, APIT) to be renewed annually.

question_text: What must a psychologist do when impaired and in a professional relationship?

options.A: Continue practicing while self-medicating with over-the-counter pharmaceuticals
options.B: Disclose full personal diagnostic details to all current clients in therapy
options.C: Delegate all clinical decision-making to administrative office receptionists
options.D: Terminate appropriately, notify client in writing, and assist with referral

explanation: Rule 510-5-.05 requires an impaired psychologist who is in an active professional relationship to terminate appropriately, notify the client in writing, and assist the client in finding alternative professional services.

question_text: What may the Board require of an impaired licensee?

options.A: Exam, records, referral to Colleague Assistance Program, rehabilitation, practice restrictions
options.B: Immediate lifetime revocation with no opportunity for rehabilitation or reapplication
options.C: Automatic criminal prosecution in superior court for reckless endangerment
options.D: Mandatory 500 hours of uncompensated community service in a public hospital

explanation: Rule 510-5-.05 authorizes the Board to require an impaired licensee to undergo physical/mental examination, produce records, refer to a Colleague Assistance Program, undergo rehabilitation, and accept practice restrictions.

question_text: What happens if an impaired licensee refuses evaluation/rehabilitation?

options.A: The Board must dismiss all pending complaints with prejudice
options.B: May constitute basis for disciplinary sanctions
options.C: The licensee is granted an automatic 12-month leave of absence
options.D: The matter is referred to the APA Ethics Committee for binding arbitration

explanation: Rule 510-5-.05 provides that refusal of an impaired licensee to submit to directed evaluation, treatment, or rehabilitation may constitute independent grounds for disciplinary action or summary suspension.

question_text: How long must adult psychological records be maintained?

options.A: Three years after the last date of service
options.B: Five years after the last date of service
options.C: Seven years after the last date of service
options.D: Ten years after the last date of service

explanation: Rule 510-5-.04 requires psychological records for adult clients to be retained for a minimum of seven (7) years after the last date of professional service.

question_text: How long must minor records be maintained?

options.A: Until age 18, regardless of when services were provided
options.B: Exactly seven years from the date of service, regardless of age
options.C: Until three years after age of majority, or at least seven years after last service, whichever is later
options.D: Five years after the minor reaches age 21

explanation: Rule 510-5-.04 provides that records of minor clients must be maintained until three years after the minor reaches the age of majority (i.e. age 21), or at least seven years after the last service date, whichever is later.

question_text: What must records include?

options.A: Identifying/contact data, fees/billing, informed consent, diagnosis/basis, plan, dates/services, interventions, assessment
options.B: Complete transcripts of all spoken dialogue and personal feelings of the therapist
options.C: Client personal tax returns and detailed credit card account histories
options.D: Photographs of the client and personal contact details of all extended family members

explanation: Rule 510-5-.04 enumerates required record components: identifying and contact information, fee/billing records, informed consent, diagnosis/clinical basis, treatment plan, dates and nature of services, interventions, and assessment results.

question_text: What must psychologists do with records after termination?

options.A: Publicly auction closed files to recover uncollected co-payments
options.B: Discard records immediately upon termination to protect client privacy
options.C: Transfer all clinical files to the Georgia Psychological Association archives
options.D: Continue to treat client information as confidential

explanation: Rule 510-5-.06 provides that the obligation to maintain client confidentiality continues indefinitely after termination of the professional relationship and after closure of records.

question_text: How many supervision hours are required per 20 hours of face-to-face clinical contact?

options.A: Minimum two hours
options.B: Minimum three hours
options.C: Minimum one hour
options.D: Minimum four hours

explanation: Rule 510-5-.06 requires a minimum of one (1) hour of individual face-to-face supervision for every 20 hours of face-to-face clinical client contact rendered by a supervisee.

question_text: How many supervisees may a psychologist supervise concurrently without Board approval?

options.A: No more than one
options.B: No more than two
options.C: No more than five
options.D: No more than three

explanation: Rule 510-5-.06 restricts psychologists from supervising more than three (3) psychological supervisees/trainees concurrently without prior written Board approval.

question_text: Who must make the diagnosis when clinical services are rendered by a supervisee?

options.A: The supervisee, with post-hoc cosignature on billing invoices
options.B: The supervising psychologist personally
options.C: The client's primary care physician
options.D: A consensus panel of practicum students

explanation: Rule 510-5-.06 mandates that the supervising psychologist personally determine and formulate all diagnoses for clients seen by a supervisee.

question_text: Who may select and interpret psychological tests in a supervisory setting?

options.A: The supervisee independently without supervisor input
options.B: Any psychometrician or testing technician employed by the practice
options.C: The psychologist only
options.D: The insurance company care manager authorizing testing hours

explanation: Rule 510-5-.06 requires that the selection and interpretation of psychological tests remain the non-delegable responsibility of the supervising psychologist.

question_text: Must a supervisee inform clients of their role and right to speak with the supervisor?

options.A: No; supervisees should present themselves as independent licensed practitioners
options.B: Only if the client specifically questions the supervisee's credentials
options.C: Only in inpatient psychiatric hospital facilities
options.D: Yes; supervisees must inform clients of their supervisory status and right to speak with the supervising psychologist

explanation: Rule 510-5-.06 requires that supervisees inform clients of their supervisory status and provide clients with the name and contact information of the supervising psychologist and their right to speak with them.

question_text: Who is responsible for supervisees' professional acts?

options.A: The supervisee carries sole legal and ethical liability as an independent adult
options.B: The supervising psychologist retains full, complete, ultimate authority and responsibility
options.C: Liability is shared equally among all faculty members of the supervisee's university
options.D: The client assumes all risk upon signing the initial intake disclosure form

explanation: Rule 510-5-.06 provides that the supervising psychologist retains full, complete, and ultimate professional authority and legal responsibility for all acts and services rendered by a supervisee.

question_text: Must a forensic psychologist personally examine the individual before testifying about psychological characteristics?

options.A: Personal examination is never required; reviewing records is always legally sufficient
options.B: Yes, unless examination is not feasible; then limit conclusions
options.C: No; forensic psychologists may testify based solely on hypothetical questions
options.D: Yes, with zero exceptions; failing to examine bars any testimony whatsoever

explanation: Rule 510-5-.08 requires forensic psychologists to conduct a personal examination before testifying regarding psychological characteristics, unless examination is not feasible despite reasonable efforts, in which case they must clarify the impact and limit their conclusions.

question_text: What standard governs court-appointed custody psychologists' good faith?

options.A: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5)
options.B: Federal Rules of Evidence Rule 702
options.C: APA's 2010 Guidelines for Child Custody Evaluations in Family Law Proceedings
options.D: Georgia Rules of Professional Conduct for Attorneys

explanation: Rule 510-5-.08 provides that court-appointed custody evaluators who adhere to the APA's Guidelines for Child Custody Evaluations in Family Law Proceedings are presumed to have acted in good faith.

question_text: Who determines whether a court-appointed custody psychologist acted in bad faith?

options.A: The Georgia State Board of Examiners of Psychologists
options.B: The complaining parent
options.C: The presiding judge of the court making the appointment
options.D: The American Psychological Association Ethics Committee

explanation: Rule 510-5-.08 states that whether a court-appointed child custody evaluator acted in bad faith is determined exclusively by the judge presiding over the case.

question_text: May a Georgia psychologist supervise someone who surrendered a license due to discipline?

options.A: Yes, automatically after a six-month waiting period
options.B: No, unless Board waives/modifies for extraordinary circumstances
options.C: Yes, provided the supervisee practices exclusively in private outpatient clinics
options.D: Yes, if the supervisee signs an agreement not to bill commercial insurance

explanation: Rule 510-5-.10 prohibits a Georgia psychologist from employing or supervising any individual who has surrendered a psychology license under disciplinary proceedings, unless the Board modifies this restriction for extraordinary circumstances.

question_text: Is failure to cooperate with a Board/national investigation a violation?

options.A: Yes; failure to cooperate with a lawful Board or national investigation constitutes an independent violation of Board rules
options.B: No; cooperation is strictly voluntary under Georgia administrative law
options.C: Only if the investigation involves felony criminal allegations
options.D: No, unless the investigator obtains a formal superior court order to compel

explanation: Rule 510-5-.10 establishes that failure to cooperate with a lawful investigation by the Board or a recognized national psychology committee constitutes an independent violation of Board rules.

question_text: How many days before limited practice must an out-of-state psychologist notify the Board?

options.A: At least 10 days
options.B: At least 5 days
options.C: At least 14 days
options.D: At least 30 days

explanation: Rule 510-9-.03 requires an out-of-state psychologist intending to practice temporarily in Georgia to submit written notice to the Board at least five (5) days prior to the start of practice.

question_text: What is the maximum days per calendar year for limited practice in Georgia?

options.A: 15 days
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 90 days

explanation: Rule 510-9-.03 limits temporary practice by an out-of-state licensee to a maximum of 30 days per calendar year.

question_text: What disaster response networks are exempt from Georgia licensure?

options.A: Any private corporate employee assistance program network
options.B: Local municipal neighborhood watch and community civic clubs
options.C: Commercial telehealth platforms providing crisis counseling for a fee
options.D: American Red Cross, ICISF, APA/Georgia Psychological Association Disaster Response Network, or other nationally recognized networks

explanation: Rule 510-9-.03 exempts out-of-state psychologists practicing as volunteer disaster responders affiliated with the American Red Cross, ICISF, APA/GPA Disaster Response Network, or other recognized disaster relief organizations.

question_text: What credentials are needed for temporary in-person practice under PSYPACT?

options.A: ASPPB IPC and PSYPACT TAP
options.B: ASPPB E.Passport and APIT authorization
options.C: CPQ and Georgia temporary license
options.D: ABPP Diploma and National Register credential

explanation: Rule 510-9-.03 provides that temporary in-person face-to-face practice under PSYPACT requires an ASPPB Interjurisdictional Practice Certificate (IPC) and PSYPACT Temporary Authorization to Practice (TAP).

question_text: How many days per year may PSYPACT psychologists practice temporarily in Georgia?

options.A: Up to 15 days per calendar year
options.B: Up to 30 days per calendar year
options.C: Up to 60 days per calendar year
options.D: Up to 90 days per calendar year

explanation: Rule 510-9-.03 and PSYPACT compact rules allow psychologists holding TAP to practice in-person in a receiving compact state for up to 30 days per calendar year.

question_text: May an unlicensed person render psychological services for a fee?

options.A: Yes, if the person discloses lack of licensure on client receipts
options.B: Yes, if registered as a life coach with the Secretary of State
options.C: No; rendering psychological services for a fee or remuneration without a valid Georgia license is unlawful
options.D: Yes, provided fees do not exceed fifty dollars per hour

explanation: Rule 510-10-.01 prohibits an unlicensed individual from rendering psychological services for a fee or remuneration in Georgia.

question_text: May an unlicensed person supervise psychological services?

options.A: Yes, in non-profit community clinics and crisis hotlines
options.B: Yes, if the unlicensed supervisor has at least 10 years of clinical experience
options.C: Yes, provided a licensed psychologist co-signs reports quarterly
options.D: No; an unlicensed person is strictly prohibited from supervising psychological services rendered by trainees or employees

explanation: Rule 510-10-.01 prohibits an unlicensed person from supervising psychological services rendered by trainees or employees.

question_text: May an unlicensed person use titles implying licensure?

options.A: No; an unlicensed person may not use titles or descriptions tending to convey the impression of psychology licensure
options.B: Yes, if the word 'consultant' is appended to the title
options.C: Yes, provided the title is used exclusively in marketing brochures
options.D: Yes, if the individual holds a master's degree in clinical psychology

explanation: Rule 510-10-.01 prohibits an unlicensed person from using any title or description tending to convey the impression that they are licensed to practice psychology in Georgia.

question_text: Who may administer and interpret psychological tests?

options.A: Any healthcare provider holding a valid Georgia medical or nursing license
options.B: Currently licensed Georgia psychologist; students/trainees under direct licensed supervision
options.C: Certified school counselors and licensed life coaches independently
options.D: Any business consultant who has completed test publisher certification

explanation: Rule 510-10-.03 specifies that psychological tests may only be selected, administered, and interpreted by a currently licensed Georgia psychologist or students/trainees under direct licensed supervision.

question_text: After how many failed EPPP attempts must additional coursework be completed?

options.A: After two unsuccessful attempts, 1 semester hour or 5 CE hours
options.B: After five unsuccessful attempts, 6 semester hours or 30 CE hours
options.C: After three unsuccessful attempts, 3 semester hours or 15 CE hours before 4th-6th retakes
options.D: After one unsuccessful attempt, 2 semester hours or 10 CE hours

explanation: Rule 510-2-.01 provides that after three failed EPPP attempts, an applicant must complete 3 semester hours of coursework or 15 CE hours before being permitted to retake the exam (attempts 4-6).

question_text: After how many failed EPPP attempts are 9 semester hours required?

options.A: After three unsuccessful attempts
options.B: After four unsuccessful attempts
options.C: After five unsuccessful attempts
options.D: After six unsuccessful attempts

explanation: Rule 510-2-.01 requires an applicant who fails the EPPP six times to complete 9 semester hours of graduate coursework before retaking the examination.

question_text: How long is an application valid after Board approval?

options.A: One year from approval/completion of postdoctoral SWE
options.B: Two years from approval/completion of postdoctoral SWE
options.C: Three years from approval/completion of postdoctoral SWE
options.D: Six months from approval/completion of postdoctoral SWE

explanation: Rule 510-2-.06 provides that an approved application for licensure remains valid for one year from the date of approval or one year from the date of completion of postdoctoral SWE.

question_text: When may the Jurisprudence exam be scheduled?

options.A: Identified or clearly recognizable as paid advertisements
options.B: After passing the national exam and while completing SWE
options.C: Submit application for reinstatement per Rule 510-7-.02
options.D: Application, 40 CE hours within two years, and penalty fee

explanation: After passing the national exam and while completing SWE. (Rule 510-2-.01)

question_text: When may the oral exam be scheduled?

options.A: After passing all exams and within 3 months of completing SWE
options.B: After passing all exams and within 6 months of completing SWE
options.C: After passing all exams and within 2 months of completing SWE
options.D: After passing all exams and within 11 months of completing SWE

explanation: After passing all exams and within 2 months of completing SWE. (Rule 510-2-.01)

question_text: How recent must the oral exam work sample be?

options.A: Generated within 3 months preceding the exam or within 6 months of most recent professional practice
options.B: Generated within 11 months preceding the exam or within 6 months of most recent professional practice
options.C: Generated within 12 months preceding the exam or within 6 months of most recent professional practice
options.D: Generated within 6 months preceding the exam or within 6 months of most recent professional practice

explanation: Generated within 6 months preceding the exam or within 6 months of most recent professional practice. (Rule 510-2-.01)

question_text: What is the maximum CE credits per biennium for Area I (Academic)?

options.D: None

question_text: What is the minimum and maximum CE credits for Area II (Group Consultation)?

options.A: No more than 20% of internship/SWE
options.B: Minimum 10, maximum 20 per biennium
options.C: Not necessarily for clinical work
options.D: Maximum 10 per course, 20 per biennium

explanation: Minimum 10, maximum 20 per biennium. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: What is the maximum CE credits for Area III (Approved Sponsored CE)?

options.A: Minimum one hour
options.B: At least one-half
options.C: 40 per biennium
options.D: No more than three

explanation: 40 per biennium. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: How many psychologists must be in a group consultation group?

options.A: 6 credits, in-person or synchronous webinar
options.B: ASPPB E.Passport and APIT authorization
options.C: The supervising psychologist personally
options.D: Minimum 3, maximum 8 licensed participants

explanation: Minimum 3, maximum 8 licensed participants. (Rule 510-8-.02)

question_text: How many ethics CE credits are awarded for a full biennium of Georgia Psychological Association Ethics Committee service?

options.B: Child welfare agency (DFCS) of county where child resides or abuse occurred, or appropriate police authority or district attorney
options.C: Immediately, but in no case later than 24 hours from the time there is reasonable cause to believe suspected child abuse occurred
options.D: An individual entrusted by agreement with a parent or guardian with the responsibility of education and supervision of a minor

explanation: An individual entrusted by agreement with a parent or guardian with the responsibility of education and supervision of a minor. (OCGA 16-6-5.1(a)(5.1))

question_text: Does professional or statutory privilege prevent mandatory reporting of elder or disabled adult abuse under OCGA 30-5-4?

options.A: No; abuse, neglect, or exploitation must be reported notwithstanding any privileged communication (except clergy confession)
options.B: Yes, provided the arrangement is documented in writing and is not clinically contraindicated
options.C: Yes, provided notice is given to the Secretary of State within 14 calendar days
options.D: Yes, if approved by a majority vote of the Georgia State Board of Examiners

explanation: No; abuse, neglect, or exploitation must be reported notwithstanding any privileged communication (except clergy confession). (OCGA 30-5-4(d))

question_text: By what means may a report of suspected disabled adult or elder abuse be submitted under OCGA 30-5-4?

options.A: No more than three supervisees
options.B: Oral or written communication
options.C: Any person under 18 years of age
options.D: Equitable alternative activities

explanation: Oral or written communication. (OCGA 30-5-4(b)(2))

question_text: Within what timeframe must a law enforcement agency forward a report of elder or disabled adult abuse to the adult protection director?

options.A: Within 12 hours of receipt
options.B: Within 48 hours of receipt
options.C: Within 24 hours of receipt
options.D: Within 72 hours of receipt

explanation: Within 24 hours of receipt. (OCGA 30-5-4(b)(3))

question_text: Under OCGA 43-39-7(8), how many days per year may an out-of-state licensed psychologist practice in Georgia without a Georgia license?

options.A: No more than 1 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided
options.B: No more than 2 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided
options.C: No more than 3 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided
options.D: No more than 30 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided

explanation: No more than 30 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided. (OCGA 43-39-7(8); Rule 510-9-.03)

question_text: Does an individual holding authority under PSYPACT need to apply for a Georgia license to practice telepsychology or temporary in-person practice in Georgia?

options.A: No; practicing pursuant to PSYPACT (Article 2 of Chapter 39) is an express statutory exception to Georgia licensure
options.B: Yes, provided full written informed consent is documented in the client record
options.C: Yes, with advance written notification to the Board and client waiver of privilege
options.D: Yes, if approved by a majority vote of the Georgia State Board of Examiners

explanation: No; practicing pursuant to PSYPACT (Article 2 of Chapter 39) is an express statutory exception to Georgia licensure. (OCGA 43-39-7(9))

question_text: Under what conditions may psychology students, trainees, or assistants engage in psychology activities without a license?

options.A: No more than 30 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided
options.B: When under direct supervision and responsibility of a licensed psychologist, without representing themselves as psychologists
options.C: American Red Cross, ICISF, APA/Georgia Psychological Association Disaster Response Network, or other nationally recognized networks
options.D: Through subpoena by the division director upon reasonable grounds, and such records are admissible in board hearings

explanation: When under direct supervision and responsibility of a licensed psychologist, without representing themselves as psychologists. (OCGA 43-39-7(7))

question_text: Who regulates psychological testing and assessment performed by licensed professional counselors and social workers in Georgia?

options.A: Fraud/deception in applying or passing exam; felony conviction; false/assumed name; habitual intemperance; negligence; violation of 43-1-19
options.B: American Red Cross, ICISF, APA/Georgia Psychological Association Disaster Response Network, or other nationally recognized networks
options.C: The Georgia Composite Board of Professional Counselors, Social Workers, and Marriage and Family Therapists has sole authority under Chapter 10A
options.D: When under direct supervision and responsibility of a licensed psychologist, without representing themselves as psychologists

explanation: The Georgia Composite Board of Professional Counselors, Social Workers, and Marriage and Family Therapists has sole authority under Chapter 10A. (OCGA 43-39-7(10))

question_text: Does the statutory definition of the practice of psychology in Georgia permit psychologists to prescribe drugs or practice medicine?

options.A: Yes, under the physician-psychologist collaborative practice exception
options.B: Yes, upon formal written petition and prior approval by the Georgia State Board
options.C: Yes, if conducted under the direct supervision of a Board-approved licensed psychologist
options.D: No; nothing in the definition shall be construed as permitting administration or prescription of drugs or infringing upon practice of medicine

explanation: No; nothing in the definition shall be construed as permitting administration or prescription of drugs or infringing upon practice of medicine. (OCGA 43-39-1(7))

question_text: Can a psychologist's description of testing as 'psychological' in nature alter the statutory definition of psychological testing under OCGA 43-39-1(6)?

options.A: No; labeling cannot alter the statutory definition requiring measurement of mental abilities/personality/brain function and diagnosing disorders
options.B: Yes, provided notice is given to the Secretary of State within 14 calendar days
options.C: Yes, provided the arrangement is documented in writing and is not clinically contraindicated
options.D: Yes, provided full written informed consent is documented in the client record

explanation: No; labeling cannot alter the statutory definition requiring measurement of mental abilities/personality/brain function and diagnosing disorders. (OCGA 43-39-1(7))

question_text: Which Georgia statute governs Board hearings for license refusal, suspension, or revocation under OCGA 43-39-13?

options.A: APA or CPA accreditation (with exceptions for I/O and international)
options.B: The Georgia Administrative Procedure Act (OCGA Title 50, Chapter 13)
options.C: Chapter 295-3 through 295-13 of the Office of Joint Secretary rules
options.D: Refuse to grant, revoke, discipline, or impose probationary license

explanation: The Georgia Administrative Procedure Act (OCGA Title 50, Chapter 13). (OCGA 43-39-13(b))

question_text: Where must an appeal of a Board decision refusing, suspending, or revoking a license be filed?

options.A: Office of State Administrative Hearings (OSAH)
options.B: Georgia Court of Appeals
options.C: Superior court of the county where the division director maintains offices (Fulton County)
options.D: Probate Court of the county of practice

explanation: Superior court of the county where the division director maintains offices (Fulton County). (OCGA 43-39-13(c))

question_text: Under what standard of review must the superior court evaluate the Board's findings of fact on appeal?

options.A: Generated within 6 months preceding the exam or within 6 months of most recent professional practice
options.B: Only those from regionally accredited institutions or that were the basis for psychology licensure
options.C: Assessment/diagnosis theories, effective treatment, consultation/supervision, evaluating efficacy
options.D: Any evidence standard: if findings are supported by any evidence, they must be accepted by the court

explanation: Any evidence standard: if findings are supported by any evidence, they must be accepted by the court. (OCGA 43-39-13(c))

question_text: What maximum civil fine may a Georgia professional licensing board impose per violation under OCGA 43-1-19?

options.A: A fine not to exceed $500.00 for each violation
options.B: A fine not to exceed $250.00 for each violation
options.C: A fine not to exceed $1,000.00 for each violation
options.D: A fine not to exceed $2,500.00 for each violation

explanation: A fine not to exceed $500.00 for each violation. (OCGA 43-1-19(d)(4))

question_text: Under OCGA 43-1-19, how may the Board obtain medical and mental health records of an applicant or licensee?

options.A: Individual differences, human development, dysfunctional behavior/psychopathology, ethics/professional standards
options.B: Through subpoena by the division director upon reasonable grounds, and such records are admissible in board hearings
options.C: No more than 30 days per calendar year, provided the other jurisdiction has equal/greater standards and notice is provided
options.D: Only uncompensated for public/nonprofit agencies serving indigent patients in underserved/critical-need areas

explanation: Through subpoena by the division director upon reasonable grounds, and such records are admissible in board hearings. (OCGA 43-1-19(c))

question_text: What is the effect of an adjudication of mental incompetence by a court on a psychologist's Georgia license?

options.A: Manufacture, distribution, trafficking, sale, or possession of controlled substance or marijuana
options.B: Biological, cognitive/affective, social, history/systems, measurement, methodology, data analysis
options.C: Automatic suspension of the license for as long as the adjudication of incompetence is in effect
options.D: Assessment/diagnosis theories, effective treatment, consultation/supervision, evaluating efficacy

explanation: Automatic suspension of the license for as long as the adjudication of incompetence is in effect. (OCGA 43-1-19(a)(9))

question_text: Does a sentence entered pursuant to a plea of nolo contendere or first-offender treatment constitute grounds for Board discipline under OCGA 43-1-19?

options.A: Only when practicing under the direct supervision of a licensed physician or psychiatrist
options.B: Only for endorsement applicants with at least ten years of continuous active licensure
options.C: Only if the psychologist has completed a minimum of two years of postdoctoral experience
options.D: Yes; both are conclusive evidence of an arrest and sentencing and constitute grounds for disciplinary sanction

explanation: Yes; both are conclusive evidence of an arrest and sentencing and constitute grounds for disciplinary sanction. (OCGA 43-1-19(a)(4))

question_text: What is the maximum number of supervisees for whom a psychologist may take primary supervisory responsibility without prior Board approval?

options.A: No more than three supervisees
options.B: No more than two supervisees
options.C: No more than four supervisees
options.D: No more than five supervisees

explanation: No more than three supervisees. (Rule 510-5-.06(3)(a)(5); Rule 510-2-.05)

question_text: What must a supervisee inform a client before providing psychological services?

options.A: Nature/procedures, risks/benefits, limits of confidentiality, fees, third parties, opportunity to ask questions
options.B: Supervisee status, supervisor name and contact info, and client right to confer with the supervising psychologist
options.C: Felony punishable by 1 to 25 years imprisonment and fine up to $100,000 (10 to 30 years if victim is under 16)
options.D: Purpose, duration, procedures, right to decline/withdraw, risks/benefits, confidentiality limits, incentives, contact

explanation: Supervisee status, supervisor name and contact info, and client right to confer with the supervising psychologist. (Rule 510-5-.06(3)(a)(4); Rule 510-2-.05)

question_text: May a psychologist withhold client records needed for emergency treatment solely because payment for services has not been received?

options.A: Yes, with advance written notification to the Board and client waiver of privilege
options.B: Yes, provided full written informed consent is documented in the client record
options.C: No; psychologists may not withhold records requested and needed for a client emergency treatment solely for nonpayment
options.D: Yes, after a mandatory waiting period of two years following service termination

explanation: No; psychologists may not withhold records requested and needed for a client emergency treatment solely for nonpayment. (Rule 510-4-.02 Standard 6.03)

question_text: When is bartering for psychological services ethically permissible under Board rules?

options.A: Activities, total hours, client/patient involvement hours, and individual supervision hours
options.B: Advance plans to transfer records and protect confidentiality if withdrawing from practice
options.C: Until three years after age of majority, or at least seven years after last service, whichever is later
options.D: Only if it is not clinically contraindicated and the resulting arrangement is not exploitative

explanation: Only if it is not clinically contraindicated and the resulting arrangement is not exploitative. (Rule 510-4-.02 Standard 6.05; Rule 510-5-.01)

question_text: What is required before recording the voices or images of clients to whom psychological services are provided?

options.A: Prior permission from the client or their legal representative
options.B: Only if disguised, consented in writing, or legally authorized
options.C: Take reasonable precautions to protect confidential information
options.D: Only information germane to the purpose of the communication

explanation: Prior permission from the client or their legal representative. (Rule 510-4-.02 Standard 4.03)

question_text: What is the distinction between 'test data' and 'test materials' under APA Standard 9.04 and 9.11?

options.A: Use of assessment instruments to measure mental abilities, personality, or neuropsychological functioning and to diagnose/evaluate mental disorders
options.B: Test data includes raw/scaled scores, client responses, and notes; test materials refers to manuals, instruments, protocols, and test questions (which must be secured)
options.C: Information and techniques sufficient to substantiate findings, including personal interviews when appropriate
options.D: Purpose, test factors, test-taking abilities, situational/personal/linguistic/cultural differences

explanation: Test data includes raw/scaled scores, client responses, and notes; test materials refers to manuals, instruments, protocols, and test questions (which must be secured). (Rule 510-4-.02 Standard 9.04, 9.11)

question_text: What professional standard applies to psychological services delivered via telecommunications technology in Georgia?

options.A: Employee is subject to employer's direction of time, manner, and method; independent contractor controls those
options.B: A written report detailing apprehension circumstances, which becomes part of the clinical record with the certificate or court order
options.C: Telepsychology must adhere to the exact same legal, ethical, and clinical standards as in-person psychological practice
options.D: When other mental health services are unavailable and they make reasonable efforts to obtain competence

explanation: Telepsychology must adhere to the exact same legal, ethical, and clinical standards as in-person psychological practice. (Rule 510-5-.07)
